examples.question_text: Maya has a gross annual income of $\$76\,800$ and allowable deductions of $\$2340$. Calculate her taxable income.

Leo earned a salary of $\$81\,450$, bank interest of $\$286.70$ and rental income of $\$12\,600$. His allowable deductions are union fees of $\$615.40$, work-related equipment costing $\$1240$ and a tax agent fee of $\$165$. Calculate his annual taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Gross income}&=81\,450+286.70+12\,600\\&=\$94\,336.70\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Allowable deductions}&=615.40+1240+165\\&=\$2020.40\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Income less deductions}&=94\,336.70-2020.40\\&=\$92\,316.30\end{aligned}$

Round down to the nearest whole dollar. The taxable income is $\$92\,316$.

examples.question_text: Ava paid $\$380$ for a work-related conference and was reimbursed in full by her employer. She also paid $\$560$ in union fees and $\$210$ for protective work shoes, both allowable deductions. Her gross annual income is $\$68\,750$. Explain why the conference fee cannot be claimed, then calculate her taxable income.
examples.solution_text:
The conference fee was reimbursed, so Ava did not personally bear the expense and cannot claim it.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Allowable deductions}&=560+210\\&=\$770\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Taxable income}&=68\,750-770\\&=\$67\,980\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Noah earns $\$2985.40$ gross per fortnight and received $\$243.85$ in bank interest for the year. His allowable deductions are a work uniform costing $\$9.60$ per week, union fees of $\$14.25$ per week and an annual charity donation of $\$180$. Calculate his annual taxable income, rounded down to the nearest whole dollar. Use $26$ fortnights and $52$ weeks per year.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual gross income}&=2985.40\times26+243.85\\&=77\,620.40+243.85\\&=\$77\,864.25\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual deductions}&=(9.60+14.25)\times52+180\\&=1240.20+180\\&=\$1420.20\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Income less deductions}&=77\,864.25-1420.20\\&=\$76\,444.05\end{aligned}$

Round down to the nearest whole dollar. The annual taxable income is $\$76\,444$.

examples.question_text: Isla's annual tax payable is $\$18\,735.60$. It is collected in equal fortnightly PAYG instalments. Calculate each instalment to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
There are $26$ fortnights in a year.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Fortnightly PAYG instalment}&=18\,735.60\div26\\&\approx\$720.60\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Ethan pays a fortnightly PAYG instalment of $\$745.25$. Calculate the total tax withheld over a full year.
Grace has a gross annual income of $\$73\,200$ and annual tax payable of $\$14\,386.50$. Tax is her only deduction. Calculate her annual net income.
Oliver's gross weekly pay is $\$1468.50$ and his weekly PAYG instalment is $\$318.75$. Tax is his only deduction. Calculate his net weekly pay.
Amelia has a gross annual income of $\$83\,200$ and annual tax payable of $\$17\,654$. Tax is her only deduction. Calculate her net monthly pay to the nearest cent.

examples.derivation: Gross income: 81450 + 286.70 + 12600 = 94336.70. Deductions: 615.40 + 1240 + 165 = 2020.40. Difference: 92316.30; rounding down gives $92,316.
The reimbursed conference expense is excluded under the supplied reimbursement condition. Allowable deductions: 560 + 210 = 770. Taxable income: 68750 − 770 = $67,980.
Annual gross income: 2985.40 × 26 + 243.85 = 77864.25. Annual deductions: (9.60 + 14.25) × 52 + 180 = 1420.20. Difference: 76444.05; rounding down gives $76,444.
18735.60 ÷ 26 = 720.60 exactly. Each fortnightly PAYG instalment is $720.60.
Annual net income: 83200 − 17654 = 65546. Monthly net pay: 65546 ÷ 12 = 5462.1666…, giving $5,462.17 to the nearest cent.
